analysis.title: GS Basics - PCs. Capex vs. FCF Strain. China Lows
key_insights: Asia overnight looks like a potential outright gross unwind. KOSPI is down about 3.5% and TWSE about 2.5%. AI winners are down 3-5% while consumer names and AI laggards catch a bid.

Amazon AWS grew 39.3% to $46bn, ahead of consensus but a little light of whisper numbers. Capex is $220bn this year and 'meaningfully more' in 2027. Management guides AWS growth above 40% in both 2027 and 2028.
Inference already accounts for well over half of AWS's AI revenue, per Amazon management, and enterprises are described as still early in using inference at scale.

Amazon's weakness is outside AWS. Advertising grew 12% to $19.6bn versus 18% expected, the first miss in seven quarters. Consumer growth was softer, Q4 sales guidance was a touch light and trailing free cash flow is negative $42bn.

The core businesses financing the AI investment cycle are under more scrutiny. Prime Day timing explains part of the Amazon ad weakness and management guides advertising back to high-teens growth in Q4, so extrapolating is probably premature.

Reddit observed that 'AI mode does not drive traffic', which raises the question of whether AI could eventually cannibalize advertising economics. The author calls it too early to conclude, since AI may also stimulate commercial search.
Intel fell more than 20% overnight and weighed on the broader semiconductor tape. Q4 revenue is guided to $15-16bn versus about $17bn expected, tied to an operational issue at an Israeli fab.

Intel's Data Centre and AI revenue grew 78% and server CPU demand exceeds what Intel can supply, while PC demand is contracting as memory inflation raises hardware costs. Manufacturing and packaging limits constrain the server CPU upside.
The read-across for PC-exposed suppliers is negative. Some may view Intel's packaging and fab bottlenecks as company specific rather than a secular break in enterprise compute demand.

Iran appears to have rejected the latest mediated overtures and restated its seven conditions for peace. Other headlines say the parties are 'very close'. Middle Eastern equities fell again even with oil lower, which suggests regional investors fear escalation.
The author has little conviction on Iran, sees a very wide range of outcomes and thinks plenty of risk premium is priced.

Hyperscaler results showed enterprise cloud consumption and contracted backlogs remain resilient. The market is now questioning balance sheet financing, multi-year ROIC and who ultimately earns the returns.

Financing constraints could eventually force capex discipline, but the author does not see it in spending intentions yet. The point where hyperscalers shift from needing capacity at almost any cost to optimizing returns on what they have built is the stated worry.

Positioning is light and sentiment bearish, so the desk expects a chop. The midterms next week, unresolved Iran and pressure on index heavyweights make adding risk difficult, with post-event periods seen as a chance to climb the wall of worry.
Side note: SHCOMP is back near its 1-year lows.

market_movers.rationale: Stock fell more than 20% overnight on a Q4 revenue guide of $15-16bn versus about $17bn expected. Server CPU demand is strong but supply is constrained and PC demand is contracting.
AWS beat consensus but advertising missed and trailing free cash flow is negative $42bn. The note treats the ad miss as partly Prime Day timing and flags funding and returns as the bigger issue.

sector_views.rationale: Intel's guide hit the broader tape and the read-across for PC-exposed suppliers is negative, but Intel's bottlenecks may be company specific.
Near-term price action stays challenging as the market digests elevated capex commitments, while contracted backlogs remain substantial.

tension_points.bull_case: Enterprise cloud consumption and contracted backlogs remain resilient. AWS grew 39.3% and management guides above 40% growth in 2027 and 2028, with inference already well over half of AWS AI revenue.
tension_points.bear_case: Core businesses financing the buildout are slowing, with Amazon advertising up 12% versus 18% expected and trailing free cash flow at negative $42bn. The market is questioning balance sheet financing and who earns the returns.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscalers shifting from needing capacity at almost any cost to optimizing returns on what they have already built, which would show up as capex discipline in spending intentions.

tension_points.bull_case: Prime Day timing explains some of Amazon's weakness and management guides advertising back to high-teens growth in Q4. AI may also stimulate commercial search activity.
tension_points.bear_case: Amazon's advertising miss follows a search miss from a peer earlier in the week, and Reddit says AI mode does not drive traffic, so AI could cannibalize ad economics.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Amazon advertising failing to return to the guided high-teens growth in Q4.

tension_points.bull_case: Intel's packaging and fab bottlenecks are company specific rather than a secular break in enterprise compute demand, and server CPU demand is so strong Intel cannot meet it.
tension_points.bear_case: PC demand is contracting as memory inflation lifts hardware costs, and the read-across for PC-exposed suppliers is negative.

theme_stances.key_argument: The market increasingly questions who earns the returns and how the investment cycle gets financed, with cash flow under pressure and financing needs rising.
theme_stances.evidence: The bigger issue is increasingly funding and returns.

theme_stances.key_argument: Server CPU demand outstrips Intel's supply while PC demand contracts on memory inflation, creating a mismatch between capacity and demand.
The range of outcomes is enormous and plenty of risk premium looks priced.
theme_stances.evidence: Very difficult to carry much conviction around this one
